entries.title: Bringing the magic: Google breaks open a bottleneck in quantum computing
entries.content:
Google Quantum AI has demonstratively opened up a key bottleneck in quantum computing: we’ve shown that “magic state cultivation” works in practice on our Willow processor, reducing errors about 40x compared to without it. This breakthrough, published today in Science, is a crucial step towards scaling up quantum computing to practical use.

The "magic state" bottleneck

Since 2004, long before quantum computing was a practical engineering pursuit, researchers have foreseen a particularly tricky bottleneck.

To achieve “universal” quantum computing and execute useful programs, you need to be able to run (and error-correct) a specific set of quantum operations. You can do this by first creating what are called "magic states," so dubbed because they can help you create the operations you need for going beyond classical computing.

But there’s a catch: creating high-quality, error-corrected magic states is incredibly resource-heavy. Some estimates have shown that up to 95% of a quantum computer’s entire capacity might need to be dedicated to making them — leaving little room for actual computing. An extra challenge is that once you use a magic state, you can’t re-use it, making magic states a scarce resource.

So for 20 years, researchers have been chipping away at this cost of magic, bringing it lower and lower.

How we made this breakthrough

In 2024, Google Quantum AI researchers Craig Gidney, Noah Shutty, and Cody Jones harnessed an idea from the literature, refined it, and developed what we now call “magic state cultivation.” Their approach promised an especially large reduction. The idea was that cultivation would act like a filter. You would inject a noisy state into a small region on a quantum chip, and then run a series of highly coordinated measurements to check for errors and remove any flawed attempts. Craig and team showed how that would let you grow, or “cultivate,” an exceptionally pure, low-error quantum state that you could simultaneously adapt into a larger, useful encoding.

On paper, it looked great. If we could make this idea actually work on our quantum hardware, it could substantially reduce the size of the quantum computer needed for practical tasks.

In practice — and on par with developing many new technologies — it required a whole series of technical innovations and engineering.

As just one example, when first testing the cultivation protocol, Google Quantum AI research scientist Emma Rosenfeld was seeing data that seemed to defy the laws of physics. After months of confusion, simulations, discussions with colleagues, and consistency checks, she found that it arose from an incorrect assumption in the team’s go-to measurement technique. Specifically, a particular kind of noise in the lab caused by electrical equipment drift and temperature variation was interfering with the benchmark’s validity. The solution required a pivot in both our theoretical and engineering approaches. The team added extra control to the system to reduce the impact of that noise, and invented a new benchmarking technique to solve the issue more fundamentally, by using cultivation as a tool to measure itself.

With this and many more algorithmic innovations and engineering solutions, we established a new state-of-the-art in quantum metrology. On Google Quantum AI's Willow processor, our protocol achieved an extraordinary 40-fold reduction in errors relative to un-cultivated states. And we got T-states with a record logical fidelity of 99.99%.

Now published in Science, this work is the first demonstration of a practical solution to one of quantum computing's most severe resource bottlenecks. It demonstrates, on real hardware, that we can efficiently create these crucial magic states.

Our findings and the future

We also took the first steps in demonstrating that Craig and others’ theories are compatible with our quantum computing architecture. We learned how to successfully switch between “color codes” (one newer type of quantum error correction, ideal for cultivation) and “surface codes” (another, more established method), grafting states from a distance-3 color code to a distance-5 surface code. Originally developed in the 2024 theory paper, this grafting protocol showed that in practice, purified states can survive and transfer smoothly inside our hardware.

Of course, we still need to demonstrate magic state cultivation at a larger scale to make it realistic for practical quantum computing, and plenty of technical challenges remain. But this achievement takes a key theoretical idea and turns it into an experimentally demonstrated reality. It brings us one step closer to our goal at Google Quantum AI: building a useful, error-corrected quantum computer to solve otherwise unsolvable problems.

entries.title: Check if a text message is a scam using Circle to Search.
entries.summary: Use Google Circle to Search to analyze suspicious texts for scams. Long-press your home button to get AI insights on messages. See how it works.
entries.content:
Scammers have gotten more sophisticated — but so have the tools we use to stop them. Circle to Search on Android can review suspicious text messages to help you identify potential scams before you click a link or share your personal information. 1

To give it a try, long-press the home button or navigation bar on your Android device to activate Circle to Search, then draw a circle around the message you're unsure about. You’ll see an AI Overview with guidance and insights including suggested next steps. If the results show red flags, consider deleting the message and blocking the number.

entries.title: How we're helping the world prepare for natural disasters
entries.summary: Our north star is simple yet ambitious: No one should be surprised by a natural disaster.
entries.content:
Today is International ShakeOut Day, when millions practice earthquake drills. Our Android Earthquake Alerts System turns smartphones into a global network that can warn people before shaking arrives, and it's expanding to more countries and regions.

When a natural disaster strikes, early warnings and trusted information help people prepare, respond, and stay safe. Earthquakes are only one part of our crisis resilience efforts at Google. Our AI models also help people prepare for other natural disasters:

  • Floods: Our flood forecasting technology provides up to seven days' notice for riverine floods for more than two billion people in 150 countries and up to 24 hours' notice for urban flash floods.
  • Cyclones: WeatherNext can predict cyclones up to 15 days out.
  • Wildfires: Near-real-time fire boundary maps are live in 34 countries, and FireSat, a global satellite constellation, is designed to detect and track fires as small as a classroom within 20 minutes once completed.

In 2025 alone, Google helped connect people with crisis information more than 10 million times per day, on average.

Our north star is simple yet ambitious: No one should be surprised by a natural disaster.

Learn more about our progress on crisis resilience and how we are working with partners and communities around the world to better prepare for natural disasters in our new Crisis Resilience white paper.

entries.title: Android earthquake alerts now available in more than 200 regions
entries.content:
A few seconds of warning when an earthquake hits can give you crucial time to take cover and protect yourself and your loved ones. To make these early warnings possible at scale, we built the Android Earthquake Alerts System — the world’s largest mobile-based earthquake detection network.

Since launching in 2021, we’ve sent over one billion alerts to help people stay safe before the shaking even starts. Today, we’re expanding the system from 98 countries and regions to more than 200 — including Panama, Guatemala and many more.

We’re also improving our latest “Be Ready” alert to give you more information in seconds. If an earthquake occurs in a region where alerts are active, Android users can expect to see one of three alerts:

  • Be Aware: A straightforward alert for estimated light shaking, letting you know an earthquake has been detected nearby.
  • Be Ready: A detailed alert for stronger shaking, alerting you to prepare to take action.
  • Take Action: A full-screen alert for moderate to heavy shaking, giving you immediate advice on how to stay safe.

We’ve built-out our Be Ready alert with new helpful guidance. In the coming months, you’ll see a map with a radius of where we’ve detected shaking, estimated earthquake magnitude, action you can take, and a button to learn more about the earthquake as information comes in.

Updated "Be Ready" alert coming soon

Our physical safety products are deeply important to us. While we hope they never get used, we’re grateful to be able to bring more information to more people when they need it most. Learn more about the Android Earthquake Alerts System and where it is active. 1 To see how we're helping communities around the world better prepare for earthquakes and other natural disasters, read our new Crisis Resilience white paper.

entries.title: 400 publications are now partnering with us on our News AI pilot program.
entries.summary: People’s information habits are evolving quickly, and platforms and publishers of all sizes are navigating these changes. To help meet this moment, we’re evolving our pa…
entries.content:
People’s information habits are evolving quickly, and platforms and publishers of all sizes are navigating these changes. To help meet this moment, we’re evolving our partnerships as newsrooms adapt to these shifts in user preferences and new technology. Since launching our News AI pilot program last year with a range of news partners, like The Washington Examiner and The Washington Post, more than 400 publications worldwide are now participating in this program.

Our newest partners range from global outlets like Axios, CNN, The Financial Times, and Forbes, to local publishers like Post and Courier, Texas Tribune, Oil City News, and Shaw Media in the U.S.

Through this licensing program, we pay participating news publications for the delivery and use of enhanced content to develop new AI features. For example, these experiences include in-depth article overviews on Google News publisher pages offering people helpful context before they click and customizable audio briefings for listeners. With clear attribution and direct links, these features build meaningful new ways for readers to connect with the sources they value.

entries.title: More ways to connect with the web from Search
entries.content:
Whether you’re coming to Search to quickly find information, explore new topics, or discover new voices, we want to make it as easy as possible for you to dive deeper and engage with the content and sources you value. We’re seeing people take advantage of tools that give them more choice: the number of people who now use our Preferred Sources feature has grown by more than 7x since the start of the year. Today, we’re announcing updates across AI Search to make exploring the web simpler, more visual, and more engaging.

1. Engage with more inline links

Inline links, which are links embedded in words or phrases in an AI response, help you dive deeper into a topic the moment you’re reading about it. We’ve made continued and substantial increases to the presence of inline links in our AI experiences. We're also launching updates to show inline links higher up in responses more frequently, helping to ensure key sources are easily clickable right when you need them.

2. Find exactly the right web page

Sometimes, there are only one or two official places on the web to complete a specific task or get the exact info you need. We'll be testing a new display in Search AI experiences to prominently surface these links in a dedicated section at the top of a response, with context about why each link is useful. With these links and additional context, you can be more confident you’ve found what you’re looking for. This expands on what we already do today to show links front and center when you’re looking to go to a particular site.

3. Discover more news and reporting

We’re starting to roll out the prominent carousels you see for timely articles in AI Search features to additional locations and languages globally. These carousels also highlight your Preferred Sources, making it easier to find coverage from the websites you value. This feature makes timely articles more visible on a wider range of queries.

4. Dive deeper with prominent links to related articles

Once you’ve gotten the lay of the land on a topic, you might want to dig deeper on interesting angles – and we want to make it easy to find links that spark your curiosity. So we’re making the links that we show at the end of some AI responses more engaging and prominent, with image thumbnails and a more clickable design.

5. Connect with creators

This week, we started testing clickable creator and publisher names on video results that link directly to their Search profiles in AI Mode. These profiles give you a quick way to learn about creators and their broader work, giving you even more context. Eligible creators and publishers can learn more about Search profiles and how to get started.

These updates help you dive further into the information you’re looking for, and we'll keep refining these experiences based on what works best.

entries.title: Making your Pixel devices last longer through design, repair, and reuse
entries.content:
Our devices should be built to last — and easy to repair when life happens. As we celebrate International Repair Day, we are reflecting on how circularity shapes everything we build. Extending the lifespan of hardware is one of the most meaningful ways to reduce e-waste and maximize the value of our technology.

Here’s a closer look at how we are making repair and reuse more accessible, dependable, and impactful.

Designing devices for repairability: The Pixel Watch & Fitbit Edge

Sustainable hardware begins with thoughtful engineering. For the Pixel Watch 4 and 5, our design and engineering teams established an ambitious repairability roadmap and identified common repair bottlenecks from the earliest stages of development.

The result is an industry-leading modular architecture that rejects the industry standard of heavily glued, unserviceable components. And according to iFixit, it's the most repairable smartwatch out there, earning a 9 out of 10 repairability score.

And this week we expanded our repairable products with the new Fitbit Edge, our first repairable fitness tracker, featuring an internal modular architecture and a replaceable battery designed to extend the life of your device.

Making it easy for you to access expert Pixel support

Great design must be backed by fast, reliable support when you need it. Here are all the ways Pixel customers can extend the life of their devices.

  • Flagship device protection: Pixel Care+ offers eligible users peace of mind with protection against cracks, spills, drops, and more.
  • My Pixel app on-device support: The Support tab in My Pixel is a hub to find solutions. Head there to run diagnostics, chat with an AI agent to troubleshoot an issue, or easily start a repair.
  • Google Store repair information hubs: We launched country-specific repair support pages that feature multiple repair solutions and transparent price estimates, helping you find the best option for their needs.
  • A new, simplified repair process: Our self-service repair program is now integrated with Your Devices, so you can quickly verify your Pixel device details and start a hassle-free repair.
  • Global walk-in repair network: Through our global network of walk-in service centers and authorized providers, you can access quick, certified repairs with genuine parts.
  • Google Store trade-in program: When it's time for an upgrade, our Google Store Trade-In Program makes it easy to exchange eligible devices for store credit, so older devices get safely refurbished or responsibly recycled.

Expanding our certified pre-owned program

The Google Certified Refurbished program keeps high-performing hardware in circulation longer, without compromising on quality or performance.

Every phone in the program is restored with genuine Google parts, updated with the latest Android software, packaged in 100% plastic-free materials, and backed by our full one-year warranty. To make sustainable upgrades even more accessible, we’re expanding the program on two fronts: we added the Pixel 9 series to our U.S. lineup at up to 45% off on the Google Store Online U.S., and we launched certified refurbished devices on the Google Store Online Japan this October.

We'll continue to invest in sustainability, product longevity, and repair to extend the lifespan of our products. And we invite you to join us in this journey: whether you are checking your device’s health via the My Pixel app, exploring repair options, or opting for a Certified Refurbished device.

entries.title: An intelligent new shopping cart
entries.summary: Images of the global cart UI, over a collage of products
entries.content:
As we build for the future of commerce, our focus spans two fronts: unlocking agentic capabilities that act on your behalf, and designing practical tools that give shoppers confidence and control. Google’s Universal Cart is built for that second track — mirroring how people actually shop today across Google, without losing track of their items, their savings, or the merchants they trust.

The Universal Cart, which we previewed earlier this year, is an intelligent shopping cart and your new hub for shopping on Google. The cart puts you in control, helping to organize your shopping, keep track of items you love from across retailers, stay on top of promos, and enjoy effortless checkout powered by the Universal Commerce Protocol (UCP). Today, Universal Cart is rolling out in the U.S. across Google Search and in the Gemini app.

The cart for all your shopping

Here are four things the new Universal Cart lets you do to stay organized and shop more confidently this holiday season.

1. Save products from multiple retailers, wherever you’re shopping on Google. Universal Cart offers a more organized alternative to tabs and screenshots. The cart saves your progress across Google so you never have to start your shopping from scratch. Let’s say you save a handbag from Steve Madden to your cart in AI Mode in Search, and later a sweater from Quince and lipgloss from Ulta Beauty in the Gemini app. Those products will be there in your cart when you come back later so you can pick up right where you left off.

2. Keep tabs on pricing or inventory changes for your entire list. The cart is built on the 60+ billion continually refreshed product listings in Google’s Shopping Graph. This allows it to proactively work for you in the background, sending notifications about price drops or when an item comes back in stock.

3. Identify hidden savings or points from your cart. The cart’s intelligent reasoning can help anticipate your needs. Say you have a couple different credit cards, but don’t know each one’s specific benefits. The Universal Cart is built on Google Wallet so it understands your card perks and can intelligently help you choose between payment methods. It’ll also show you relevant promo codes right from the cart.

4. Make seamless, trusted purchases when you’re ready to buy. In online shopping, trust is everything. You can securely check out with Google Pay in just a few taps with many of your favorite stores right in the cart, or you can transfer your items directly to the merchant’s cart to finish buying on their site. Try these simplified checkout experiences with merchants like Nike, Sephora, Target, Ulta Beauty, Walmart, Wayfair, and many Shopify merchants. Either way, you will receive direct confirmations and customer support from the merchant, and they will remain the seller of record.

As the holiday season kicks into high gear, the Universal Cart is just one way we’re giving shoppers the convenience and smarts they need to make the best shopping choices.

entries.title: TIME has named Google SynthID one of the Best Inventions of 2026.
entries.summary: TIME named Google SynthID a Best Invention of 2026 for its groundbreaking approach to AI watermarking and verification.
entries.content:
TIME has named Google SynthID to its annual list of Best Inventions.

As generative AI makes digital media more realistic, knowing how content was made helps you navigate the web with confidence.

Google SynthID embeds an invisible, durable digital watermark into AI-generated images, audio, video, and text at the moment of creation, without altering the quality. To date, SynthID has watermarked more than 180 billion images and videos and 240,000 years of audio. We also recently announced SynthID Bio, bringing SynthID’s watermarking technology to synthetic biology.

To help people identify AI content, verification tools are built directly into Google Search, the Gemini app, and Chrome. You can also use the SynthID Detector to check content from Google and our partners.

Together, these tools help give you more transparency and context around the content you encounter online. You can read more about this and other inventions on TIME’s website.

entries.title: Data-backed secrets to smarter holiday shopping
entries.summary: A graphic containing the text "When to Buy" interspersed with isolated consumer products against a plain white background. The word "When" is written in a large black sans-serif font on the upper left, and "to Buy" is on the bottom right.
entries.content:
Finding the perfect holiday gift shouldn't feel like a guessing game. To take the stress out of your shopping, we analyzed historical promotional patterns, Search trends, and discount data across U.S. merchants on Google. The result is our When to Buy Guide, a research-backed roadmap showing when holiday discounts may hit their peak, based on data from last year.

Here are a few tips and findings to help you shop smarter. For the full list of pricing trends and insights into our last-minute gifting habits, read the complete When to Buy Guide. You'll also discover which parent we shop for later, and which state claims the most last-minute shoppers.

  • Snag your scent before the holiday rush: If you're eyeing a perfume or cologne for someone on your list, shop early. Fragrance discounts don’t typically increase as Christmas approaches, and the volume of fragrance deals drops off sharply, so waiting until late December may not offer lower prices — and could leave you with fewer options. Strategize by buying fragrances within the first two weeks after Black Friday weekend for the best deals and inventory selection.
  • Reconsider the Black Friday handbag frenzy: If you’re on the lookout for the perfect handbag at the best price, consider holding off on buying during Black Friday weekend. Target mid-December to balance a high discount with a decent selection of styles, or wait until late December if you just want the lowest price on remaining inventory.
  • Shop early for travel accessories, but later for suitcases: While travel accessories see their best deals in November, major items, such as large luggage and suitcases, don't typically hit their deepest markdowns until clearance sales in late December. With this in mind, consider buying travel accessories and packing cubes on Black Friday, but wait until late December for deep clearance discounts on large suitcases, though there may be less selection.
  • Want a tech toy deal? Wait for it: Unlike traditional electronics, categories like motorized tech toys show some of their steepest markdowns emerging in the final weeks of December. If electronic toys are on your kids’ wish lists, consider holding out until the final shopping stretch to unlock surprise last-minute savings. If you wait to buy, keep an eye on holiday shipping deadlines, unless you plan on shopping in-store.

These trends should help you shop smarter this holiday season, but pricing and inventory can vary from year to year, so think of them as general guidance rather than absolute guarantees.
